blocks.explanation:
Paanch A.M.s "insert" karne ka matlab hai \(\sqrt{2}\) aur \(\frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) ke darmiyan paanch aise numbers rakhna ke saaton numbers mil kar A.P. ban jayein.
Is A.P. mein 7 terms hain: pehla \(\sqrt{2}\), aakhri (7th) \(\frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\).
Plan: \(a_7 = a_1 + 6d\) se \(d\) nikalenge, sab ko ek hi denominator \(6\sqrt{2}\) par likhenge, phir \(d\) bar bar jama karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_1 = \sqrt{2}\), \(a_7 = \frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) (beech mein 5 A.M.s)
Humein find karna hai: \(A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_5\).
Tareeqa: \(\sqrt{2}, A_1, \ldots, A_5, \frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) ek A.P. hai jis ke 7 terms hain; \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) mein \(n = 7\) rakhenge. Paanch A.M.s + do kinare = 7 terms, is liye \(n = 7\).

\(d\) ke liye equation banayein
\[a_7 = a_1 + 6d\]
\[\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} + 6d\]
Kyun: Pehle term se 7th term tak jane ke liye \(d\) chhe (6) dafa jama hota hai, saat dafa nahi.
Dhyan dein: paanch A.M.s ke liye \(6d\) aata hai (\(n + 1\) qadam), \(5d\) nahi; yeh sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(d\) nikalein
\[6d = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} - \sqrt{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[d = \dfrac{13}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: Minus karne ke liye dono ka denominator ek jaisa chahiye. \(\sqrt{2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\) hai, kyunke \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\). Phir \(15 - 2 = 13\) aur dono taraf 6 se divide kiya.

Pehle term ko \(6\sqrt{2}\) ke denominator par likhein
\[\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{12}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: Ab \(d\) ka denominator \(6\sqrt{2}\) hai. Agar pehla term bhi isi denominator par ho to har dafa \(d\) jama karna sirf numerator mein 13 jama karna reh jata hai. Is se har qadam par rationalise karne ki mehnat bach jati hai.

\(d\) paanch dafa jama karein
\[A_1 = \dfrac{12 + 13}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{25}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_2 = \dfrac{38}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{19}{3\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_3 = \dfrac{51}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{17}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_4 = \dfrac{64}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{32}{3\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_5 = \dfrac{77}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: Numerators: \(12 + 13 = 25\), \(25 + 13 = 38\), \(38 + 13 = 51\), \(51 + 13 = 64\), \(64 + 13 = 77\). Jahan numerator aur 6 mein common factor tha wahan chhota kiya: \(\frac{38}{6} = \frac{19}{3}\), \(\frac{51}{6} = \frac{17}{2}\), \(\frac{64}{6} = \frac{32}{3}\). 25 aur 77 ka 6 se koi common factor nahi.

Tasdeeq: ek qadam aur aakhri term tak
\[A_5 + d = \dfrac{77 + 13}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{90}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Agar sab sahi hai to \(A_5\) mein ek \(d\) aur jama karne se aakhri diya hua term \(\frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) aana chahiye. \(90 \div 6 = 15\), bilkul wahi aaya. Is ka matlab har qadam sahi tha.
